data.case_title: Tax residency self-certification request – Beispiel Direktbank
data.title: Request to confirm tax residency (CRS self-certification) from Beispiel Direktbank
data.summary: Beispiel Direktbank AG asks Grace Mensah to complete and return a tax residency self-certification form under the Common Reporting Standard (CRS) by 29 October 2025, because the bank's records show a German address but a telephone number registered in Ghana. If the form is not received by then, the bank says it will report the account to the tax authorities of both countries.
data.explanation: German banks are legally required to check where customers are tax-resident (CRS) and can ask for a self-certification form when records look inconsistent, as here with a German address but a Ghanaian phone number. If genuine, fill in the enclosed form and return it to the bank by the stated date; otherwise the bank says it will report the account to tax authorities in both Germany and Ghana. Because the letterhead name does not match the legal entity named in the footer, call the bank on a number you already know (not one from this letter) to confirm the request is real before sending any personal information. If the deadline shown has already passed, contact the bank directly to ask how to proceed.
